Problem Domain:
Financial Services, Banking, Fraud Detection, Anomaly Detection, Real-Time Systems (Simulated), Machine Learning, Data Visualization.

Project Description:
This project focuses on building an AI-driven system for detecting potentially fraudulent banking transactions in near real-time. It utilizes Pandas for efficient data manipulation and feature engineering on transaction streams, Scikit-learn's Isolation Forest algorithm for unsupervised anomaly detection (identifying transactions that deviate significantly from normal patterns), and Streamlit to create an interactive web dashboard for visualizing transaction data, flagged anomalies, and model insights. While true real-time processing often requires specialized streaming infrastructure (like Kafka, Flink), this project will simulate the real-time aspect by processing transactions in mini-batches or reading from a simulated stream, focusing on the integration of feature engineering, anomaly detection with Isolation Forest, and interactive visualization for fraud analysis.

Frameworks Used:

  • Core Data: Pandas, NumPy
  • Machine Learning: Scikit-learn (IsolationForest, StandardScaler, metrics)
  • Web Dashboard: Streamlit
  • Visualization: Plotly (integrated well with Streamlit), Matplotlib, Seaborn
  • Data Simulation/Streaming (Conceptual): Potentially kafka-python for a more realistic simulation, or simpler file/generator-based streaming.
  • Configuration: YAML or Streamlit secrets.

Dataset:
Access to real banking transaction data is highly restricted due to privacy and security concerns. We will use a publicly available, anonymized dataset often used for fraud detection research, such as the "Credit Card Fraud Detection" dataset from Kaggle (originally from ULB).

  • Source: Kaggle: Credit Card Fraud Detection
  • Characteristics: Contains transactions made by European cardholders over two days in September 2013. Features V1-V28 are principal components obtained via PCA (to anonymize sensitive data), plus Time (seconds elapsed between transaction and first transaction) and Amount. The target variable is Class (1 for fraud, 0 for normal).

Use Cases:

  1. Real-Time Transaction Scoring: Assign an anomaly score to each incoming transaction based on the Isolation Forest model.
  2. Fraud Alerting: Flag transactions with anomaly scores exceeding a predefined threshold for review by fraud analysts.
  3. Interactive Analysis: Allow analysts to use the Streamlit dashboard to explore flagged transactions, view transaction details, analyze feature distributions for normal vs. anomalous transactions, and potentially provide feedback on alerts (labeling true/false positives).
  4. Pattern Discovery: Identify characteristics of transactions flagged as anomalous, potentially revealing new or evolving fraud patterns.
  5. Threshold Tuning: Use the dashboard to visualize the impact of different anomaly score thresholds on the number of alerts generated (trade-off between detection rate and false positives).

Full Development Lifecycle (Corporate View):

  1. Requirements & Use Case Definition (3-5 weeks): Define the scope (types of transactions, channels), specific fraud scenarios to target, latency requirements for scoring (near real-time vs. batch), desired model performance metrics (precision, recall at specific thresholds), and requirements for the analyst dashboard (visualizations, interactions, feedback mechanisms).
  2. Data Acquisition & Understanding (4-7 weeks): Identify and access relevant data sources (transaction logs, customer data, device information, potentially third-party risk signals). Perform exploratory data analysis (EDA) to understand transaction patterns, feature distributions, and existing fraud labels (if available). Assess data quality and availability.
  3. Feature Engineering (6-10 weeks): Develop features relevant for fraud detection. Examples: transaction frequency (per card, per merchant, per IP), amount deviations (from user average, merchant average), time-based features (time since last transaction, time of day), location-based features (if available), velocity checks, potentially graph-based features (connections between users/merchants).
  4. Model Selection & Training (5-8 weeks): Choose appropriate anomaly detection algorithms (Isolation Forest is specified, but others like Local Outlier Factor (LOF), One-Class SVM, or autoencoders could be considered). Train the model(s) on historical data (typically using only normal transactions for unsupervised methods like Isolation Forest, or using labeled data if available for supervised/semi-supervised approaches). Optimize hyperparameters.
  5. Real-Time Simulation & Scoring Engine (6-9 weeks): Develop the component that simulates receiving transactions, applies feature engineering, and calls the trained model to generate anomaly scores. Handle data scaling consistently between training and scoring. Optimize for efficient processing of mini-batches.
  6. Dashboard Development (Streamlit) (5-7 weeks): Design and build the interactive Streamlit dashboard. Include visualizations for transaction monitoring, anomaly lists, feature exploration, threshold analysis, and potentially feedback mechanisms.
  7. Integration & Testing (4-6 weeks): Integrate the scoring engine with the dashboard. Test the end-to-end flow with simulated data. Validate model performance on a hold-out set. Test dashboard usability and responsiveness.
  8. Deployment & Monitoring (4-6 weeks): Deploy the scoring engine and dashboard (e.g., using Docker, cloud services). Set up monitoring for system health, data ingestion, model prediction distribution (to detect drift), and alert rates. Implement a feedback loop for model retraining based on analyst labels.
  9. Operational Use & Refinement (Ongoing): Fraud analysts use the dashboard for monitoring and investigation. Collect feedback, monitor model performance, retrain models periodically, and continuously refine features and detection logic based on evolving fraud tactics.

# --- Filename: real_time_fraud_detection_dashboard.py ---

import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import joblib # For saving/loading sklearn models
import time
import logging
import os

# ML/Data Handling
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

# Visualization
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.graph_objects as go

# Configuration
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(module)s - %(message)s")

# --- Constants & Config ---
MODEL_PATH = "./models/isolation_forest_model.joblib"
SCALER_PATH = "./models/scaler.joblib"
DATA_SOURCE = "https://storage.googleapis.com/download.tensorflow.org/data/creditcard.csv" # Or local path
FEATURES = [f    V{i}     for i in range(1, 29)] + [ Amount  ] # Features to use for detection
SIMULATION_BATCH_SIZE = 50 # Number of transactions to process per update
SIMULATION_DELAY_SECONDS = 2 # Pause between batches
DEFAULT_ANOMALY_THRESHOLD = -0.1 # Initial threshold for Isolation Forest score (lower scores are more anomalous)

# --- Model Loading --- 
@st.cache_resource # Cache model & scaler loading
def load_model_and_scaler(model_path: str = MODEL_PATH, scaler_path: str = SCALER_PATH):
    """Loads the pre-trained Isolation Forest model and scaler."""
    if not os.path.exists(model_path) or not os.path.exists(scaler_path):
        st.error(f"Model ({model_path}) or Scaler ({scaler_path}) not found. Please train first.")
        # In a real app, trigger training or provide instructions
        # For this example, we might need a dummy model/scaler or stop execution
        # Let's try to train if not found (requires the full dataset)
        logging.warning("Model/Scaler not found. Attempting to train...")
        try:
            df_full = load_fraud_data(url=DATA_SOURCE) # Reload full data
            if df_full is None:
                 raise FileNotFoundError("Could not load data for training.")
            model, scaler = train_model(df_full)
            # Save them
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(model_path), exist_ok=True)
            joblib.dump(model, model_path)
            joblib.dump(scaler, scaler_path)
            logging.info("Model and scaler trained and saved.")
            return model, scaler
        except Exception as train_err:
             st.error(f"Failed to train model automatically: {train_err}")
             return None, None
    try:
        model = joblib.load(model_path)
        scaler = joblib.load(scaler_path)
        logging.info("Isolation Forest model and scaler loaded successfully.")
        return model, scaler
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"Error loading model/scaler: {e}")
        return None, None

# --- Data Loading (using function from dataset section) ---
# We load the full data once for simulation purposes
@st.cache_data # Cache the raw data loading
def load_simulation_data(url: str = DATA_SOURCE) -> Optional[pd.DataFrame]:
    df = load_fraud_data(url=url)
    if df is not None:
        # Keep original index if needed, or reset
        df = df.reset_index().rename(columns={"index": "original_index"})
        return df
    return None

# --- Model Training (Example - Run this offline usually) ---
def train_model(df: pd.DataFrame, model_path: str = MODEL_PATH, scaler_path: str = SCALER_PATH):
    """Trains Isolation Forest and Scaler (run offline)."""
    logging.info(f"Training Isolation Forest on {len(df)} samples...")
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X = df[FEATURES]
    X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)

    # Isolation Forest parameters (tune these based on validation)
    # contamination=    auto     or a small float (expected fraud rate)
    # n_estimators, max_samples etc.
    model = IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, max_samples=    auto    , contamination=    auto    , 
                            random_state=42, n_jobs=-1)
    model.fit(X_scaled)
    logging.info("Training complete.")
    return model, scaler

# --- Prediction/Scoring --- 
def predict_anomalies(model: IsolationForest, scaler: StandardScaler, data: pd.DataFrame) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Generates anomaly scores and predictions."""
    if data.empty:
        return np.array([]), np.array([])
    X = data[FEATURES]
    X_scaled = scaler.transform(X)
    # decision_function: lower scores are more anomalous
    scores = model.decision_function(X_scaled)
    # predict: returns 1 for inliers, -1 for outliers (anomalies)
    # predictions = model.predict(X_scaled) # Returns -1 for anomalies, 1 for normal
    return scores # Return scores for thresholding

# --- Streamlit App Layout --- 
st.set_page_config(layout="wide", page_title="Real-Time Fraud Detection Dashboard")
st.title("🏦 Real-Time Banking Transaction Fraud Detection")

# --- Load Model & Data ---
model, scaler = load_model_and_scaler()
simulation_data = load_simulation_data()

if model is None or scaler is None or simulation_data is None:
    st.error("Initialization failed. Cannot proceed.")
    st.stop()

# --- Sidebar Configuration ---
st.sidebar.header("Configuration")
anomaly_threshold = st.sidebar.slider(
    "Anomaly Score Threshold", 
    min_value=-1.0, 
    max_value=0.5, 
    value=DEFAULT_ANOMALY_THRESHOLD, 
    step=0.01,
    help="Lower scores indicate higher anomaly likelihood. Transactions below this threshold are flagged."
)

run_simulation = st.sidebar.button("Start/Continue Simulation")
stop_simulation = st.sidebar.button("Stop Simulation")

# --- Simulation State Management ---
if     transaction_index    not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.transaction_index = 0
if     displayed_data   not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.displayed_data = pd.DataFrame()
if     running  not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.running = False

if run_simulation:
    st.session_state.running = True
if stop_simulation:
    st.session_state.running = False
    # Optionally reset index or clear data on stop
    # st.session_state.transaction_index = 0
    # st.session_state.displayed_data = pd.DataFrame()

# --- Main Area --- 
placeholder = st.empty() # Placeholder for dynamic updates

if not st.session_state.running:
    st.warning("Simulation stopped. Click     Start/Continue Simulation    to begin.")
    # Display last known state if needed
    if not st.session_state.displayed_data.empty:
         with placeholder.container():
             st.header("Last Simulation State")
             st.dataframe(st.session_state.displayed_data.head(100), use_container_width=True)
             # Add summary plots from last state if desired
    st.stop()

# --- Simulation Loop --- 
start_index = st.session_state.transaction_index
end_index = min(start_index + SIMULATION_BATCH_SIZE, len(simulation_data))

if start_index >= len(simulation_data):
    st.success("Simulation finished: All transactions processed.")
    st.session_state.running = False
    st.stop()

# Get next batch
new_batch = simulation_data.iloc[start_index:end_index]

# Score the new batch
if not new_batch.empty:
    anomaly_scores = predict_anomalies(model, scaler, new_batch)
    new_batch[    anomaly_score   ] = anomaly_scores
    new_batch[    is_anomaly  ] = anomaly_scores < anomaly_threshold

    # Prepend new batch to displayed data (most recent first)
    st.session_state.displayed_data = pd.concat([new_batch, st.session_state.displayed_data], ignore_index=True)
    # Limit displayed history size (optional)
    st.session_state.displayed_data = st.session_state.displayed_data.head(5000) 

# Update transaction index for next iteration
st.session_state.transaction_index = end_index

# --- Display Updates --- 
with placeholder.container():
    st.header("Live Transaction Feed")
    st.write(f"Processing transactions {start_index} to {end_index-1}. Threshold: {anomaly_threshold:.2f}")

    # Display table with highlighting
    st.dataframe(st.session_state.displayed_data.head(100).style.apply(
        lambda row: ["background-color: #FFCCCC" if row[    is_anomaly  ] else "" for _ in row], axis=1
    ), use_container_width=True)

    st.header("Analysis")
    col1, col2 = st.columns(2)

    current_anomalies = st.session_state.displayed_data[st.session_state.displayed_data[    is_anomaly  ]]
    current_normal = st.session_state.displayed_data[~st.session_state.displayed_data[    is_anomaly  ]]

    with col1:
        st.subheader("Anomaly Score Distribution")
        if not st.session_state.displayed_data.empty:
            fig_hist = px.histogram(st.session_state.displayed_data, x="anomaly_score", 
                                    color="is_anomaly", nbins=50, 
                                    title="Distribution of Anomaly Scores",
                                    color_discrete_map={True:     #EF553B , False:    #636EFA })
            fig_hist.add_vline(x=anomaly_threshold, line_dash="dash", line_color="black", annotation_text="Threshold")
            st.plotly_chart(fig_hist, use_container_width=True)
        else:
             st.write("No data processed yet.")

    with col2:
        st.subheader("Transaction Amount: Normal vs. Anomaly")
        if not current_anomalies.empty and not current_normal.empty:
            # Use Plotly graph objects for overlayed histograms or box plots
            fig_box = go.Figure()
            fig_box.add_trace(go.Box(y=current_normal[    Amount  ].clip(0, 5000), name=  Normal  , marker_color= #636EFA )) # Clip amount for better viz
            fig_box.add_trace(go.Box(y=current_anomalies[    Amount  ].clip(0, 5000), name=  Anomaly , marker_color= #EF553B ))
            fig_box.update_layout(title="Transaction Amount Distribution (Clipped at 5000)")
            st.plotly_chart(fig_box, use_container_width=True)
        else:
             st.write("Not enough data for comparison yet.")

    st.subheader("Flagged Transactions Details")
    if not current_anomalies.empty:
        st.dataframe(current_anomalies[[col for col in current_anomalies.columns if col !=     is_anomaly  ]].head(50), use_container_width=True)
        # *** Pro Feature: Add feedback mechanism ***
        # selected_indices = st.multiselect("Mark as True Fraud:", options=current_anomalies.index)
        # if st.button("Submit Feedback"): handle_feedback(selected_indices)
    else:
        st.write("No transactions flagged as anomalies with the current threshold.")

# --- Auto-refresh Logic --- 
time.sleep(SIMULATION_DELAY_SECONDS)
if st.session_state.running:
    st.rerun()

To Run This Example:

  1. Save the code above as real_time_fraud_detection_dashboard.py.
  2. Ensure you have the required libraries: streamlit, pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, joblib, plotly, requests.
  3. (Optional but Recommended) Download the creditcard.csv dataset and place it in the same directory or update LOCAL_DATA_PATH.
  4. Run the Streamlit app from your terminal: streamlit run real_time_fraud_detection_dashboard.py
  5. The app will attempt to load/download the data and train/load the model on first run if needed.
  6. Use the sidebar controls to start/stop the simulation and adjust the anomaly threshold.

Where to Go From Here (Improvements):

  1. Real-Time Infrastructure: Replace the simulation with actual real-time data ingestion using Kafka, Kinesis, or similar, and a stream processing framework like Flink, Spark Streaming, or Faust.
  2. Advanced Feature Engineering: Incorporate more sophisticated features, especially those requiring stateful computation (e.g., rolling aggregates over user history, time since last transaction per card/merchant, graph features).
  3. Supervised/Semi-Supervised Models: If reliable fraud labels are available (even for a subset), train supervised models (XGBoost, LightGBM, Neural Networks) or semi-supervised models for potentially better performance than purely unsupervised Isolation Forest.
  4. Model Explainability: Integrate SHAP or LIME to explain why a specific transaction was flagged as anomalous by the Isolation Forest (or other models).
  5. Feedback Loop: Implement a robust mechanism for analysts to label flagged transactions (true fraud/false positive) and use this feedback to periodically retrain or fine-tune the model.
  6. Ensemble Methods: Combine Isolation Forest with other anomaly detection algorithms (e.g., LOF, One-Class SVM) into an ensemble for more robust detection.
  7. Scalability: For high-volume transaction streams, ensure the scoring engine and feature engineering steps are highly optimized and potentially distributed.
  8. Dashboard Enhancements: Add more sophisticated visualizations (e.g., network graphs if using graph features), time-based analysis plots, and more detailed drill-down capabilities for analysts.
  9. Automated Threshold Tuning: Develop a method to automatically adjust the anomaly threshold based on desired alert rates or feedback data, rather than manual adjustment.
  10. Champion-Challenger Framework: Implement a system to test new models (challengers) alongside the currently deployed model (champion) on live data before promoting a new model.
